---
title: "One day, open science – the housing-audit case"
subtitle: "Four parts of ninety minutes, with a facilitator"
---
The [case study](../../cases/housing/index.qmd), which presents the original study, the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the SCORE replication on which every format of the case is built, is the place to start.

This is the one-day course on the housing-audit case with open research in the foreground. It works on one field experiment, in which emails that differed only in the name that signed them were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, and on a claim of the original authors (OAs) that five analysts reanalysed for Multi100. In the morning you meet the arguments and the evidence on the credibility of social science, the three kinds of repetition that go under the word 'replication', and the archives and registries in which open research keeps its materials; then you read the paper and its claim with the five analysts, and write the estimand statement behind the claim. In the afternoon you reproduce one of the five reanalyses, whichever you choose, and find out what a reproduction needs besides data and code. You end on the replication that tested the claim with new data, read its preregistration, and fill in a preregistration block of your own without running it. The day has no menu of specifications and sends nothing to a class chart; the [one-day course on methods](../housing-one-day-methods/index.qmd) does both.

The day is taught mainly in the [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd), a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser, with nothing to install. If you have installed R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), the downloadable workspace holds the same tasks and gives the same numbers. The day runs as four parts of ninety minutes, with breaks of thirty, sixty and thirty minutes between them. The class writes its estimand statements and its reproduced values in the chat and sends them at the same moment, so the day needs a facilitator. The same case is also taught as a [short session](../housing-short/index.qmd) and as a one-day course on [data tools](../housing-one-day-data-tools/index.qmd).

| | What happens | Length |
|---|---|---|
| [Before the day](before.qmd) | Read the case study and open the browser lab once; install R, an IDE and the workspace if you want to work there. | about an hour, more with the installation |
| [Part 1 – Credibility and open research](part-1.qmd) | What a claim is for, why the field talks of a crisis, the three Rs and the practices of open research, SCORE and Multi100, and the software, archives and registries of open research; then you open the browser lab. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 2 – The claim and its estimand](part-2.qmd) | The paper and the five analysts, two studies on why analysts disagree, and the estimand statement, which you write in Task 2. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 3 – Reproduction](part-3.qmd) | You reproduce one of the five reanalyses, find out what a reproduction needs, and reproduce a second one if there is time. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 4 – Replication and preregistration](part-4.qmd) | The new audit and its preregistration, the public record of the case, and a preregistration block that you fill in without running it. | 90 minutes |
| [After the day](after.qmd) | Where to go next. | as you like |
